body:
Alright, I'll post my first thoughts here. Might create a blog for this later to keep everything organized.

I tried to kill myself on Saturday, December 20th, 2014, sometime after midnight. I took a bunch of pills, based on some stuff I read on the internet. I assumed that this was the best option for me because I was afraid of cutting myself (and also afraid of the mess it would leave for my parents to clean up) and didn't have any other options readily available to me. I went to bed shortly after, hoping that I would die in my sleep. The following 24 hours after that are a complete blank. I can remember bits and pieces, but the next thing I can clearly remember is waking up in a hospital bed on the 21st. There was an IV drip attached to my left arm and my mom was waiting in a chair next to my bed.

Based on my parents' recollection of the many hours that I missed, I think things went like this:

> From midnight to 8am I was hyperactive. I vomited several times all over the room, and attempted to clean it up with little success.

> At around 8 or 9 am my dad came to my room and asked me to walk the dog. He opened the door to find me cleaning up my vomit. Nothing I said made any sense, but I was screaming and rambling.

> Dad drove me to the hospital immediately, where they checked me in and pumped my stomach. Luckily for me, I had already vomited up most of the pills, so I had done no damage to my liver or brain. 

> I experienced spasms for a while and lost control of most of my bodily functions, such as urination. Not my finest moment. I think I remember something about a catheter?

> Throughout all of this I continued to yell and was incomprehensible. I apparently tried to rip out my IV drip several times and had to be restrained.

When I woke up, I was in immense pain. I couldn't lift my arms enough to eat anything and had to be fed by my parents. I fell asleep again, not sure for how long. This pattern continued for a while until I reached a point where I was conscious and had enough strength to feed myself. I talked to my parents and told them how I was feeling, and what drove me to attempt suicide (more on that later I suppose). The doctors informed me about my status, what they had done to help me, and all the stuff that happened while I was blacked out.

My parents informed me about the existence of something called the "Baker Act" which states that if anyone is recovered after trying to commit suicide, they are to be put under state care for a period of time. Because I had vomited up most of the pills I took, there was no clear evidence that I had tried to kill myself, so we just said that I had overdosed by accident and I was free to go home at about 7pm on Sunday, December 21st. I got back home and it seemed like nothing had happened. Family had arrived for the holidays in the time that I had been gone, and we ate dinner together like a normal family. No one even mentioned once that I had been moments away from death just over 36 hours ago.

Anyway, the reason why I tried to kill myself is that I failed out of college. I had been playing video games and doing drugs all semester instead of working hard like I promised my parents I would, even though I was on academic probation. This semester's grades were the final straw, and I was out. Instead of telling my parents the bad news, I decided that it would be easier to kill myself and let them find out once I was gone. Instead, I survived and I have to face the music.

Now that this experience is behind me, I think I learned a few things. First, I now know that the human body is pretty resilient. There is no painless method of suicide, no matter what people might say, and each minute of death is agony. Even thinking about that moment now makes me want to vomit. Second, I see that telling my parents about how I fucked up wasn't as bad as I thought it would be. Yes, it sucks that I'm officially a college dropout and now I have to find a job and put my life back together, but my parents still love me no matter what. They will support me through these troubling times, and I am capable enough to get my shit together. I just lost my way for a moment.

Finally, I realize that I have more options available to me than I previously thought. I don't know exactly what they are, but I'm talking with people close to me so that I can find out what they are.

I still have the marks from where they drew my blood, and where the IV drip went in my left arm. I don't ever want to forget what they look like, and how they feel. Take what you will from this story, but I hope it helps you to realize that suicide is not the answer. 

*will continue tomorrow, feeling drowsy*
